chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, all from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Let those whom your right hands possess, and those who have not yet reached puberty from you, seek permission three times, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you.
And whoever has reached puberty, let him not enter upon his mother, nor his sister, nor his maternal aunt, nor anyone besides that, except by permission.
So do not give permission until they have greeted, and the greeting is obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said: And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Let your servant seek permission from you when he has reached puberty during three times of privacy, when he enters any one of them, even if his room is in your house.
And let him seek permission from you after the evening prayer which is called Al-Atamah, and when it is morning, and when you put off your clothes from the midday heat.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only commanded that for privacy, for these are times of inattention and privacy.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times and conditions for seeking permission in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elaborates on the Quranic command for *istidhan* by specifying three distinct times of privacy (*awrat*)—after the night prayer (*'Atamah*), at dawn, and at midday—when family members must seek permission to enter. The hadith emphasizes that greeting (*salam*) is an act of obedience to God and that permission should not be granted until the greeter has been acknowledged, ensuring modesty and preventing surprise encounters during moments of undress or intimacy.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, altogether from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Let them seek permission, those whom your right hands possess, and those who have not yet reached puberty, three times from you just as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Commanded you; and the ones who have attained puberty, so he should neither enter into (chamber of) his mother, nor the (chamber of) his sister, nor the (chamber of) his maternal aunt, nor the (chamber of) anyone besides that, except by permission.
So do not give permission until they have greeted, and the greeting is in obedience to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.

He (the narrator) said: ‘And Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let your servant seek permission to you when he has attained puberty during three times of privacy, when he enters the (chamber of) anyone of them, even though his room is inside your house.
And let him seek permission after the evening which is called Al-Atmat, and when it is the morning, and when you put-off your clothes from the backs.
But rather, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Commanded with that for the privacy, for these are timings of inattention and privacy’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id all from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al- Mada’iniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Your slaves and those of you who have not yet gained feeling of carnal desires must ask for your permission three times as Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has commanded.
Those who have gained feeling of carnal desire must not enter the place of his mother, sister and maternal aunt or others without permission
and you must not give permission unless he offers you Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) in obedience to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’

He (the narrator) has said that abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Your servants who have gained feeling of carnal desires must ask you for permission during three times of privacy if they come to you in such times even if their home is the same as your home.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘They must ask you for permission after al-‘Isha’ called al-‘Atmah, in the morning and at noontime when you undress.
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has commanded as such because of privacy and at these times one is unaware and in retreat.’”
